# Search — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for search when someone is looking for something among many and knows a word for it: a list of records, a documentation site, a settings page. It is a whole form rather than a bare input, so submitting works with the keyboard's Enter as well as the button, and it carries a search landmark so it is findable by assistive tech. Put it above what it filters and keep the results where the list already was, so the thing being searched never moves away from the field doing the searching.

### Usage

**Do**

- `label` names the landmark, `placeholder` hints the empty field — keep them different jobs, not two copies.
- Run the query in `onSearch`, mirror keystrokes in `onValueChange` — submit and change are separate moments.
- Use the trailing slot for the one control that belongs with search (avatar, overflow) — the clear action renders beside it.

**Don't**

- Don't pass `onSubmit` or `onChange` — the type omits them on purpose; `onSearch` and `onValueChange` are the handlers.
- Don't render results inside the bar — search finds, what it finds is the page's business.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bar | resting | comp.search.bar | surface-container-high, full pill, h-14 |
| Clear control | hover | sys.state.hover-state-layer-opacity | 8% on-surface-variant wash over the 40px clear button |

### FAQ

**Why is there no `onSubmit`?**

The type strips it deliberately — the form submits internally and reports through `onSearch`. Passing `onSubmit` will not typecheck, which is the point.

**Search or text field with a button?**

A landmark with submit-and-clear semantics means search. Free entry with validation means a text field.

## Native

### Features

Reach for search when the input IS a query: filtering a list, finding a record, looking something up. It keeps two callbacks apart, which is the part worth understanding before you wire it. `onValueChange` fires as the text changes and `onSearch` fires when the query should RUN — so a live filter and a submit-on-enter UI are the same component, and neither has to guess at the other's timing. `label` is the field's name. Note the underlying `value`/`onChangeText` are omitted from the inherited props: this component owns them and renames them.

### Usage

**Do**

- `label` names the field — the placeholder is separate and defaults to the same wording.
- Keep `onValueChange` (live change) and `onSearch` (the query to run) separate — they are two different moments.
- Use the docked bar for in-screen search; full search with results wants its own route.

**Don't**

- Don't submit from `onValueChange` — wait for `onSearch`, or every keystroke runs a query.
- Don't hide the clear control's label — it is the only control in the bar besides entry.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bar | resting | theme.color.surfaceContainerHigh | surfaceContainerHigh stadium, full pill, minHeight 56 |
| Bar border | focused | theme.color.primary | 1px primary border only while focused |
| Query text | resting | theme.color.onSurface | onSurface; placeholder is onSurfaceVariant |

### FAQ

**Search or text field?**

A query that runs (`onSearch`) with a clear control means search. Free entry with validation means a text field.

**How does this differ from the web search?**

Same contract (`label`, live change vs run, `onSubmit`/`onChange` stripped in favor of `onSearch`/`onValueChange`). The docked stadium and the focus-only border are drawn to the same roles natively.
